Reporter, Ibrahim Patel and Cameraman Chris from the South Africa Broadcasting Corporation took a video interview of Swamishri. Q: What is the purpose of inaugurating the mandir and of what significance will it be to the residing Hindus? Swamishri: God has created the world. For the purpose of worship, the murti of God is established in a mandir. People can also offer prayers to Him and be blessed with peace of mind, good thoughts and be inspired to perform good deeds. Secondly, because of the hectic day to day activities, one is left with lingering thoughts in the mind at the end of the day. By having darshan of the Lord in the mandir, experiencing the arti and listening to the sound of bells, one’s mind becomes pacified. The mandir makes a person good. By inspiring devotion towards God, a person becomes free of his base nature, evil qualities and worldly desires and attains God’s divine abode. The mandir preserves character and righteous feelings in a person. And through the holy sadhus residing in the mandir, one gets guidance and inspiration. So through the mandir, one is exposed to and blessed with the benefits of one’s culture, dharma, scriptural reading and association with sadhus. This is the significance of mandirs and that is why they are created. Q: What is your message for the new Millennium? Swamishri: As we are approaching the new Millennium, there is one very clear statement that today man has become corrupt in so many ways. He is thinking more and more about the ways and means to attain mundane happiness. And he does this at the cost of inflicting pain and loss to thousands of people. We see a great greed for power regardless of the misunderstanding and conflict it spawns. New researches and discoveries are made to destroy people. People produce and peddle drugs and alcohol to harass mankind, to make it miserable and destroy it. For the New Year one should endeavor to free oneself from addictions, vices and base nature. (swabhavas). Man should strive to earn money rather than kill someone for it. May people respect and love each other. We also wish that there should be projects that inspire peaceful coexistence and publication of wholesome literature. To enhance faith in God more mandirs should be established, people should study the holy scriptures, respect and love the holy saints - when such feelings arise in people then the country will benefit and progress all the more..."

Despite the fact that Swamishri was recovering after the previous day's bout of temperature, he had engaged himself in a meeting today. During lunch, a sadhu requested, "During illness you have to take rest. How can you get rest when you get engaged in one meeting after another?"
Swamishri replied, "Do you consider only sleeping as a form of rest? Look I am sitting here and am very much at ease. See how restful it is."
A sadhu added, "But one has to strain one's mind in a meeting."
Another sadhu elaborated, "Conducting meetings during illness is strainful for both body and mind. You have to think to make decisions. It is all stressful."

Swamishri replied, "One feels the stress if one takes it upon himself. Look, I just take it and put it away like this. (Swamishri took a towel from one side and placed it on the other side of his sofa.) I entrust it all to Maharaj. So where is the burden or stress! No matter what number of meetings and discussions I have, I hand it over to Maharaj. People live in tension because they burden themselves with their own worries and that of others'. And do I have any tension! People come with their pains and problems to me, but I do not take it upon my head. I simply entrust it like this. The moment I lie down I go to sleep instantly... Maharaj is the all-doer."

In spite of all his efforts in the Sanstha's activities, Swamishri's working strategy of entrusting everything to Shriji Maharaj and believing Him to be the all doer is the secret of his success and unfading experience of bliss.
A spiritual discourse should be listened to thoughtfully and with attention. One should also reflect upon every word.

250 devotees had pilgrimaged on foot from Gandhinagar to Amdavad (22 km), departing at 11.00 p.m. The devotees chanted the Swaminarayan dhun during the 7 hr pilgrimage.
Mrugesh Parmar, a teenager, had performed 2,500 prostrations from his home in Sabarmati to the mandir in Shahibaug (7.5 km).
Many devotees had pilgrimaged on foot from Randheja to Amdavad mandir (27 km).

15 Aug 2002, Amdavad

165 students of Akshar Purushottam Chhatralay, Vidyanagar, were blessed by Swamishri for having performed various austerities for one month: 120 observed dharna-parna, 5 did khatras, 36 stayed on liquid only, 8 did shishu chandrayan and 1 dharna- parna with liquid only.
Four balaks pilgrimaged on foot from Nikol to the Swaminarayan Mandir, Shahibaug (10 km).
With the floods in Surat, Swamishri remained in contact with BAPS sadhus at the Surat Mandir, guiding them and praying for the waters to abate.

This morning, prior to his puja, while Swamishri was engaged in Thakorji’s darshan he instructed to start chanting the Swaminarayan dhun for the flood waters to recede and no further loss of lives and damage to property occurs. Sadhus and devotees chanted dhun before Thakorji till 12 noon. Then the chanting continued from 12.00 noon to 4.00 pm in the assembly hall. And finally the dhun was continued till 7.00 pm before Thakorji in the mandir.

At 10.45 am Swamishri got news that the water level in Surat Mandir was rising. Swamishri reassured the sadhus that everyone was praying for the waters to subside and for no further loss of lives in the city. In the evening, on Swamishri’s instruction, 20 BAPS volunteers of Valsad, formerly fishermen, set off towards Surat with a large motorboat, food packets, drinking water and other relief materials for distribution. Swamishri had also instructed sadhus at Navsari mandir to prepare food packets.
At 7.00 pm Swamishri attended the satsang assembly during which the balaks-kishores of UK made several stage presentations.

Swamishri blessed the assembly after his morning puja, “To serve the world people become doctors, engineers and acquire other qualifications, but Yogiji Maharaj said that Satsang is the college of brahmavidya. God has blessed us with a human birth, so we should live and endeavour in such a way that God and his Sadhu are pleased and grant us moksha. Human birth is not for enjoying the worldly sense pleasures. Our culture teaches us to respect our parents, teachers and guests.” Swamishri further added that one should not keep bad company, and as satsangis follow the Shikshapatri and understand the knowledge of Akshar-Purushottam according to the Vachanamrut.
